transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Just avoid heavy work, lifting, or strenuous jobs for a month.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it’s safe to continue using them unless you’ve been told otherwise. If you’re running low, your GP should be able to provide more.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thanks. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light can be normal while your eyes adjust, and if things just seem brighter, sunglasses outside can help. But if it is significant pain in bright light, or the eye is red and painful, that is not normal and may need checking.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for explaining that. One last question, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it is still blurry, or getting worse, we may need to check it.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thanks for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all of your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass
